course_name_original: Laboratory for Computer Control and Automation of Measurement Systems
course_name_en: Laboratory for Computer Control and Automation of Measurement Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Understand basic concepts of mechatronic systems and electric circuits.
Understand basic concepts of continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems.
Understand the principles of actuators and their drives, emphasis on electric motors.
Understand the principles of sensors, sensor interfaces, and measurement systems.
Understand digital controllers, emphasis on Arduino microcontrollers.
Ability to acquire, store and process data.
Analysis and synthesis of data and information, with the use of the necessary technology.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of mechatronic systems. Parts of mechatronic system. Power and signal flow. Feedback. Interfacing. Electric circuit elements. Electric circuit analysis. Power variables.
Lab instrumentation: Power supplies. Measurements of voltage and current. Use of breadboards, digital multimeters, oscilloscope, power supplies.
Signals & systems: Continuous-time and discrete-time systems and signals. Signal discretization. Analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion. PWM signals. Frequency response. Filters.
Introduction to control systems: Modeling dynamic systems. Transfer function, poles and zeros. Closed loop control systems. Root locus. PID controllers.

Sensors: Sensor types for various variables (position, velocity, acceleration, angle, angular velocity, distance, pressure, temperature, humidity, force, torque, inclination, light intensity). Basic characteristics of sensors. Measurement systems. Sampling theorem.

Actuators: Principles of electromechanical conversion, Types and characteristics of electric motors. Torque-speed curve. Models of DC motors. Motor drives and controllers. Actuators for electric, hydraulic, pneumatic and thermal systems.

Digital controllers and microcontrollers. Digital controllers, embedded systems, internet of things. Intro to computer architecture. Optic isolation. Communication protocols. Microcontroller architecture. Arduino microcontrollers.
Arduino programming. Syntax and flow control. Variables, functions and libraries. Implementing digital logic and difference equations. Applications in control and signal processing.
teaching_methods: Laboratory exercises with the use of computer to control measurement systems and data acquisition
